questions.cardText:
[History] Why did France sell its territory to the U.S. in the Louisiana Purchase?
A. To fund its war efforts in Europe
B. To prevent British control of the territory
C. To gain diplomatic support from the U.S.
Answer: A. In 1803, France sold approximately 828,000 square miles (about 2,145,000 square kilometers) of territory to the U.S., as Napoleon Bonaparte needed funds for his military campaigns in Europe. Also, France’s inability to suppress a revolt in Haiti may have diminished its interest in maintaining vast American territories.
questions.de: 1803 verkaufte Napoleon das Louisiana-Territorium an die Vereinigten Staaten – wofür brauchte er das Geld?
questions.en: In 1803 Napoleon sold the Louisiana territory to the United States; what did he need the money for?
questions.answerDe: Für seine Kriege in Europa (den bevorstehenden Krieg gegen Großbritannien)
questions.answerEn: His wars in Europe (the coming war with Britain)

timeline.labelEn: France agrees to sell the Louisiana territory to the United States (Louisiana Purchase treaty)
timeline.labelDe: Frankreich verkauft das Louisiana-Territorium an die Vereinigten Staaten (Vertrag über den Louisiana Purchase)

questions.notes: Card broadly right but simplified: Wikipedia names France's failure to suppress the Saint-Domingue (Haiti) revolt and the prospect of renewed war with the United Kingdom as what prompted the sale, and notes Napoleon's need for funds; option B is also partly true, since Louisiana would have been easy prey for a British invasion. Area per Wikipedia: 828,000 sq mi (2,140,000 km²; card says 2,145,000). Treaty signed April 30, 1803 at the Hôtel Tubeuf in Paris (same page).

questions.cardText:
[Musicology] Which of the following scales is used in “Happy Birthday”?
A. Aeolian B. Dorian C. Ionian
Answer: C.
questions.de: Welchen Modus, benannt nach einem altgriechischen Volksstamm und gleichbedeutend mit der heutigen Dur-Tonleiter, verwendet die Melodie von „Happy Birthday to You“?
questions.en: Which mode, named after an ancient Greek people and equivalent to today's major scale, does the melody of “Happy Birthday to You” use?

timeline.labelEn: Patty and Mildred J. Hill publish “Good Morning to All”, the melody of “Happy Birthday to You”
timeline.labelDe: Patty und Mildred J. Hill veröffentlichen „Good Morning to All“, die Melodie von „Happy Birthday to You“

questions.notes: Card correct: Wikipedia's score of the song is in G major using only that scale's notes, and the Ionian mode is the major scale (Wikipedia: Ionian mode, named after the Ionian Greeks by Glarean, 1547).
